definitions.explanation: Entrusting a task, responsibility, or goods to another person or organization.

examples.japanese: {業務|ぎょうむ}を{外部|がいぶ}に{委託|いたく}する。
examples.english: To outsource work to an external party.

examples.japanese: {販売|はんばい}{委託|いたく}{契約|けいやく}を{結|むす}ぶ。
examples.english: To enter into a consignment sales contract.

examples.japanese: {研究|けんきゅう}を{大学|だいがく}に{委託|いたく}した。
examples.english: We commissioned the research to a university.

notes:
{委託|いたく} means entrustment or consignment - delegating tasks or goods to another party.

WORD FORMATION:
{委|い} (entrust) + {託|たく} (entrust, consign) = entrustment

GRAMMAR:
Used as noun and する verb: {委託|いたく}する (to entrust, outsource)

BUSINESS USES:
- {業務|ぎょうむ}{委託|いたく}: outsourcing (of work/operations)
- {委託|いたく}{販売|はんばい}: consignment sales
- {委託|いたく}{契約|けいやく}: consignment contract
- {委託|いたく}{料|りょう}: commission fee
- {委託|いたく}{先|さき}: outsourcing destination

COMMON PATTERNS:
- AにBを{委託|いたく}する: to entrust B to A
- {外部|がいぶ}に{委託|いたく}する: to outsource externally
- {研究|けんきゅう}を{委託|いたく}する: to commission research

RELATED TERMS:
- {外注|がいちゅう}: outsourcing (more casual)
- {委任|いにん}: delegation (of authority)
- {託|たく}す: to entrust (verb)
- アウトソーシング: outsourcing (loanword)

NOTE:
{委託|いたく}{販売|はんばい} (consignment sales) means goods remain owned by the supplier until sold.
